Chapter 12: Simon the Zealot and Judas—Zeal and Loyalty
Picture Simon. His life was shaped by a deep, burning passion. As a Zealot, he was all about resisting oppression, never backing down from what he believed was right. But when Simon joined this new community, something incredible happened. That fierce drive—the same energy that once fueled his anger—started to change. Instead of turning outward in violence, his zeal found a new direction. He learned how to channel that intensity into compassion, and into building something that lasted.
Then there’s Judas. Now, not Judas Iscariot, but the one they sometimes called Thaddeus or Lebbaeus. He doesn’t get much attention—often overshadowed by the other Judas. But if you look closer, his story is all about quiet loyalty. Judas was the guy asking thoughtful questions, honestly trying to understand, and sticking around, even when others walked away. That kind of steady faithfulness? It’s easy to overlook, but it’s incredibly powerful.
When you think about Simon and Judas together, they show us something important. Passion and loyalty—when they’re grounded in love—can be some of the most positive forces in our lives. Most of us know what it’s like to be pulled by strong convictions, or to wrestle with what loyalty really means. Simon and Judas prove that you can hold deep beliefs and still choose peace over conflict.
Maybe you’ve felt torn by intense emotions, or struggled with divided loyalties. If so, their stories are for you. They’re a reminder that transformation is real. Even the strongest passions can be turned toward healing, toward building bridges instead of walls. And that’s something we all need to remember.
